name: Andrej Karpathy
role: Founding member of OpenAI; former head of AI at Tesla
note: Builds GPTs from scratch on camera; Zero to Hero is the best first course in deep learning

name: Chris Olah
note: Founded Distill; his essays on what neural networks learn are the clearest writing in the field

name: Lilian Weng
role: Co-founder; former head of safety systems at OpenAI
note: Lil'Log: long-form surveys of diffusion models and agents and RL that stay current

name: Sebastian Raschka
org: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
note: Writes the code-first explanations that bridge papers and practice; Ahead of AI newsletter

name: Andrew Ng
note: Taught more people machine learning than anyone; his Stanford CS229 lectures are still the baseline

name: Yann LeCun
role: Founder; professor; former chief AI scientist at Meta
note: Convolutional networks and the case against pure autoregression; argues publicly and in detail

name: Demis Hassabis
role: Co-founder and CEO; Nobel laureate in chemistry
note: AlphaGo to AlphaFold; the lab that keeps turning games and science into general methods

name: Yoshua Bengio
role: Professor; founder of Mila and LawZero
note: Deep learning pioneer and Turing laureate; now the most careful public voice on what safe AI requires

name: Sergey Levine
note: Robot learning and offline RL; his CS285 lectures are the standard deep RL course

name: Chelsea Finn
note: Meta-learning and imitation for robots; co-leads the push toward general robot policies

name: Pieter Abbeel
note: Deep RL for manipulation; hosts The Robot Brains podcast with the people building robots

name: Russ Tedrake
note: Underactuated Robotics and Robotic Manipulation: free courses that teach the control theory behind it all

name: Daniela Rus
note: Soft robots and liquid neural networks and self-driving; runs the largest robotics lab in the US

name: Marc Raibert
org: Boston Dynamics and the RAI Institute
note: Forty years of legged robots from the MIT Leg Lab to Atlas; now runs a research institute on robot intelligence

name: John Preskill
note: Coined NISQ; his lecture notes are the free graduate course in quantum information

name: Scott Aaronson
note: Shtetl-Optimized: quantum complexity explained without hype and with the hype called out

name: Michael Nielsen
role: Research fellow; co-author of the standard textbook
note: Co-wrote Nielsen and Chuang; Quantum Country is the best interactive introduction

name: Peter Shor
note: Shor's algorithm and the first quantum error-correcting code; the reason the field has a goal

name: Jay Gambetta
note: Runs the roadmap from Qiskit to fault tolerance; the most public view into building real machines

name: Scott Manley
note: Explains every launch and failure with the orbital mechanics behind it; the field's best explainer

name: Tim Dodd
note: Long-form explainers on rocket engines and launch systems; interviews the people who build them

name: Casey Handmer
note: Essays on why Starship changes everything and what solar does to energy; first-principles and numerate

name: Jonathan McDowell
note: Tracks every object launched since 1957; the General Catalog is the field's reference dataset

name: Sara Seager
role: Professor of planetary science and physics
note: Exoplanet atmospheres and the search for life; her Exoplanet Atmospheres is the textbook

name: Jennifer Doudna
org: UC Berkeley and the Innovative Genomics Institute
note: Co-invented CRISPR genome editing; the IGI publishes what is coming next in editing

name: David Baker
org: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design
note: Protein design from Rosetta to RFdiffusion; the lab's tools are open and the papers are the field

name: George Church
note: Genome sequencing and synthesis and dozens of companies; the broadest view of what biology can build

name: Derek Lowe
note: Twenty years of honest commentary on drug discovery: what works and what fails and why

name: Eric Topol
note: Ground Truths: reads every paper that matters in medicine and AI and tells you which ones do

name: Niko McCarty
note: Essays on the history and engineering of biology; the best writing on synthetic biology for builders

name: Karl Deisseroth
note: Optogenetics and CLARITY: the tools that let you control and see circuits in a living brain

name: Ed Boyden
note: Co-invented optogenetics and expansion microscopy; builds the tools the rest of neuroscience uses

name: Edward Chang
note: Decoded speech from brain activity; the clinical lab closest to a working speech neuroprosthesis

name: Tom Oxley
note: Stentrode: a brain-computer interface implanted through blood vessels; furthest along in human trials

name: Matt Angle
note: High-channel-count implants aimed at speech; the engineering-heavy end of the BCI field

name: Jim Keller
note: Designed chips at AMD and Apple and Tesla; his interviews are the best education in how CPUs get made

name: Dylan Patel
note: The deepest public analysis of fabs and accelerators and who is winning; the industry reads it

name: Ben Eater
note: Builds a computer on breadboards from gates up; the clearest path from transistor to CPU

name: Jon Y
note: Video essays on the history and economics of the chip industry; from EUV to TSMC to memory

name: Matt Venn
org: Tiny Tapeout and Zero to ASIC
note: Makes it possible to tape out your own chip for a few hundred dollars; the on-ramp to real silicon

name: Onur Mutlu
note: Memory systems and computer architecture; every lecture of his courses is online in full

name: Lisa Su
note: Turned AMD around with chiplets and Zen; her keynotes are the clearest view of where compute is going

name: Dennis Whyte
role: Professor; former director of the Plasma Science and Fusion Center
note: Led the high-field path to fusion that became SPARC; his MIT lectures explain why it can work now

name: Bob Mumgaard
note: Building SPARC and ARC; the company most likely to put fusion power on the grid first

name: Jesse Jenkins
note: Models how the grid gets to zero carbon; Net-Zero America and the REPEAT project come from his lab

name: Hannah Ritchie
role: Deputy editor; author of Not the End of the World
note: Energy and climate by the numbers; the charts the rest of the field quotes

name: Eric Drexler
role: Author of Engines of Creation and Radical Abundance
note: Named the field and set its agenda; molecular manufacturing from first principles

name: Chad Mirkin
role: Professor; director of the International Institute for Nanotechnology
note: Spherical nucleic acids and dip-pen lithography; has founded more nanotech companies than anyone

name: Angela Belcher
note: Uses engineered viruses to grow batteries and materials; biology as a nanomanufacturing tool

name: Paul Alivisatos
note: Colloidal nanocrystals and quantum dots; the chemistry behind displays and bioimaging and solar
